what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the tools in tools/match-picks: what each tool does, what it takes and gives back, and how it runs.

payload.label: Tally a community's match picks
payload.job: Show how a community picked the winner of each match (the split by choice), what the result was, and how one person's own picks turned out
payload.description: Give the records of the matches (pick-match: matchId, label, startsAt, choices of { choiceId, label }), the picks (match-pick: matchId, pickerId, choiceId, createdAt) and the results (match-pick-result: matchId, winningChoiceId, summary, resolvedAt). Each match comes back by start time with every choice's count and whole percent (rounded, so the percents may not add to 100), the winning choice once there is a result (the latest result record counts) and, with picker_id, that picker's own choice. A picker who changed their pick counts once, for the latest pick. With picker_id the answer also lists that picker's picks newest first with the match and choice in words, the result summary, whether the pick was right once the match has a result, and whether a later pick replaced it. Free picks only: this tool reads records and moves no money. To keep wording out of a prompt or a result summary (for example talk of money), check the text with tool:check-pick-copy and the list the person gives.

rows.description: The records, each as { payload } or the record itself

picker_id.description: A person's id, to mark their own picks and give their history

matches.description: Each match: { match, totalPicks, result, userPick, choices: [{ choiceId, label, pickCount, percentPicked, selectedByUser, winner }] }

history.description: With picker_id: { pick, matchLabel, choiceLabel, resultSummary, correct, superseded } newest first

provenance.source: ported from the match-picks package (the pick split, results and personal history)

payload.label: Check a pick prompt or result for wording the person does not want
payload.job: Check the words of a free pick prompt, its choices or a result summary against the wording the person does not want used (for example talk of money) before they are written
payload.description: Give the texts to check, each as { field, text }, and banned_terms: the person's own list of words and phrases. Nothing is shipped as a default list. A term is found anywhere in a text in any letter case (so a short term also matches inside a longer word); a phrase written with spaces matches any run of white space. Returns passed and, for each hit, the field, the term and a message. An empty list passes everything. Refuses texts or terms written wrongly.

field.description: Where the text goes, for example label

banned_terms.description: The words and phrases not to use

provenance.source: ported from the match-picks package (the regulated-money copy guard, with its word list made an input)
